Mô tả

``` ```css .card { } /* Block: component đứng độc lập */ .card__title { } /* Element: bộ phận, không tồn tại ngoài block */ .card--featured { } /* Modifier: biến thể của block */ .card__btn--ghost { } /* Modifier của element */ ``` Cái nó giải quyết: selector lồng sâu (`.sidebar .card h3 span`) rất dễ vỡ khi đổi cấu trúc DOM, và specificity leo thang không kiểm soát. answer_en:
BEM is a **class naming** convention that makes each class state which component it belongs to and what role it plays. ```html

Title

Description

``` ```css .card { } /* Block: a standalone component */ .card__title { } /* Element: a part that only exists inside the block */ .card--featured { } /* Modifier: a variant of the block */ .card__btn--ghost { } /* Modifier of an element */ ``` What it solves: deeply nested selectors (`.sidebar .card h3 span`) break whenever the DOM changes, and specificity escalates out of control. BEM keeps every selector at **a single class**, so specificity stays flat and overrides are predictable. **Note 1 — there is no `block__el1__el2`.** Elements do not nest in the name. A card containing an avatar is `.card__avatar`, not `.card__header__avatar`; anything deeper should become its own block. **Note 2 — a modifier never stands alone.** `class="card--featured"` without `card` is wrong; a modifier only *adds* to the base. **When BEM is unnecessary:** projects on CSS Modules, styled-components or Tailwind already have their own isolation — layering BEM on top only lengthens names without solving anything more
